video_title: Mark Cuban on Analytics vs. the Eye Test & The Future of Sports

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban on the Mavericks' 2011 championship sweep of the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: That's easy when we swept y'all in 2011 to win a championship.

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Carr
text_blocks.text: What give us just what one of your favorite memories of those battles?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: That's easy when we swept y'all in 2011 to win a championship.

text_blocks.speaker: David Carr
text_blocks.text: We try to forget that one.

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban recalls a painful early loss against the Lakers
quotes.excerpt: We were up 30 going into the fourth quarter and I'm thinking, yeah boy, we got this.

text_blocks.speaker: David Carr
text_blocks.text: What is your lowest Laker moment?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: Early on after I bought the team, I think it was my second year. We hadn't beat the Lakers in LA in like 12 years or something crazy. And we were up 30 going into the fourth quarter and I'm thinking, yeah boy, we got this. Who loses a 30-point lead? I never seen that. Kobe got hot and it was over. It was the worst, it was the worst.

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban supports a salary floor in baseball to help small-market teams
quotes.excerpt: A salary floor should be implemented. Maybe then you don't lose a Mookie Betts if you're Boston.

text_blocks.speaker: David Carr
text_blocks.text: I believe that a salary floor should be implemented. Maybe then you don't lose a Mookie Betts if you're Boston. You don't lose a Freddy Freeman if you're Atlanta. What are your thoughts on that?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: I grew up in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania and I've been a Pirates fan since my first breath. My whole family and all my friends have been Pirates fans. And literally just for us to be 82 and 80 this season feels like an accomplishment. So when you talk about a need for a salary floor in baseball, yes, I agree. But it's going to be interesting because people always say, why don't you buy the Pirates? Why don't you buy the Pirates? Well, it takes somebody to sell them. And I'm not really a baseball guy, just a fan. But what I would tell people, if you owned a sports team and you were told that you could make $25 million a year, but you had to let people yell at you 24/7, would you take that job? And that's what it's like to be an owner of like a small market team that's not playing to win. Or trying, I shouldn't say not playing to win, because when you don't have the revenue like maybe the Pirates don't, then you've got to try to be smarter. And you've got to draft, you've got to draft right and develop right. And so, getting Paul, we've done some really smart things. But yeah, I do think that the Dodgers have a huge edge just in how they can go out and get players.

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban on balancing analytics with the eye test and team culture
quotes.excerpt: You always have to use analytics to try to get an edge. But you also have to add the eye test.

text_blocks.speaker: David Carr
text_blocks.text: What percentage of you says, no, it's all analytics? Let's just leave the emotion out of it and what part of it is just like, no, let's just see how the guy feels?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: For me, it's always been you always have to use analytics to try to get an edge. You always want to be smarter. But you also have to add the eye test and you also have to add the culture test. Every team has chemistry and culture and you have to know as an owner, manager, general manager exactly what your chemistry and culture is for your organization. And if you know that by pulling that guy, you might be living up to analytics but he's going to be pissed and he's going to be throwing his glove and he might take it out on the bat boys, you better accommodate the culture first. But on the flip side, if your culture is, look, I've been very communicative with all of our players, the whole organization, they understand that we're going to pull this guy, even though he may seem fresh, he may have more in him, because we know over the course of 162 games, this is what's going to happen and we're not in this just to win one game, we're in this to win a championship, so we have to look at the bigger picture.

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban on the financial pressures of owning a small-market sports team
quotes.excerpt: They're trying to keep up with the Joneses literally in terms of lifestyle.

text_blocks.speaker: David Carr
text_blocks.text: Do you think that most owners are in this thing because they love it or are they in it because of the bottom line?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: Every owner is different. I love the game. To me, the best part about owning the Mavs was going out there and getting up shots before games when the players are out there. But there are a lot of guys in the NBA, like in baseball and football, where it's a business and that's their choice. You can't take it away from them. But every sport is different. In the NFL, pretty much every team makes money, maybe one or two exceptions. And because they're making money, they should be able to invest where they need to invest. But then some of those same, the NFL is particularly different because you don't see a lot of those owners selling. And what that why that's important is, in a lot of cases, this is the money they live off of. So they need to make money and they need to put that in their pocket and they're trying to keep up with the Joneses literally in terms of lifestyle. And so it's a catch-22 for them. Do I put it in my pocket so I can keep up with everybody personally or do I put it into the team?

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban on Las Vegas as a premier sports destination
quotes.excerpt: Las Vegas, they're going to be the world's team. Whoever has a franchise in Las Vegas, you are the world's team.

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Carr
text_blocks.text: Get me excited about what's happening in Vegas.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: Las Vegas, they're going to be the world's team. Whoever has a franchise in Las Vegas, you are the world's team because it's the one truly tourist destination from people around the world. So you're going to get a lot of people coming from everywhere that are excited about baseball that may not have been exposed to it before. So I think there's a lot of reasons for A's fans and particularly new A's fans in Vegas to be excited. I think they're going to do a lot of great things and the stadium is just insane.

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban on how AI will revolutionize sports coaching and player development
quotes.excerpt: All the grunt work that every coach in every sport has ever had to do, AI can do better, faster, cheaper.

text_blocks.speaker: David Carr
text_blocks.text: What does the next 5 to 10 years look like with AI and tech in sport?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: All the grunt work that every coach in every sport has ever had to do, AI can do better, faster, cheaper. So much of it is reviewing plays, doing analytics of determining what coach runs what in what circumstance, how does a pitcher play this? AI tracks things that you can't remember. What was a quarterback's tendencies? What's a pitcher's? What's a hitter's tendency? Before you used to have somebody in the video room manually track all that stuff. Look at every minute of video. AI speeds up all of that. So it's nearly in real time. So by the time you get to the locker room at halftime, rather than having a limited amount of things, or by the time the manager is deciding whether or not they're going to go out to the mound, they've already got all this analysis of everything that's been going on. And it's going to get even better and where it will make the biggest difference is with health.

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban on using AI to prevent sports injuries
quotes.excerpt: Where it will make the biggest difference is with health. AI tracks things that you can't remember.

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
text_blocks.text: Where it will make the biggest difference is with health. Like in the NBA, you probably saw a lot of the injuries, right, with the ACLs and everything. And there's a lot of research that says, if you pulled a hamstring or if you are a calf problem, you are going to probably have, oh shit, I'm spacing. Achilles, yeah. So you're probably going to tear your Achilles, right? And so with AI, we're like, I invested in this company that, this guy named Brian, and he literally takes video of all athletes while they're running, while they're performing, and he can use AI to just compare them one step versus another step. And it's called Oraco. And by being able to just notice these little differences, you can start to see trends. Because you know a lot of times, the adrenaline's flowing, your mind's moving, you're not feeling shit during a game, but after the game, you pay the price, right? You know, so you can you know, so you're going to see AI used a lot more so that you can look for some of these things. And I think that'll change a lot of the way that the trainers and the medical directors deal with players before, during and after games.

quotes.speaker: Mark Cuban
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Cuban on his legacy as a father
quotes.excerpt: My kids, just being a good dad, because that's the most important to me.

text_blocks.speaker: Derek Carr
text_blocks.text: What does Mark Cuban want to be remembered for?

text_blocks.speaker: Mark Cuban
